t.3.20.1: Seeing Śūrpaṇakhā fallen before him once again, Khara, out of anger, spoke in clear words to her who had come for the sake of ruin.
t.3.20.2: But just now I dispatched those valiant blood-drinking rākṣasas to do what is dear to you; why, then, is there weeping again?
t.3.20.3: They are devoted to me, deeply attached to me, and always intent on my welfare; even if they strike, they must not be slain, for they would never fail to carry out my command.
t.3.20.4: What is this? I wish to hear the reason why you once again writhe on the ground like a snake, crying out, “Alas, O lord!”
t.3.20.5: Why do you lament like one without a protector, when I, your protector, stand here? Rise, rise up, do not be afraid; let this despondency be cast aside here.
t.3.20.6: Thus addressed and consoled by Khara, the formidable one wiped her tearful eyes and spoke to her brother Khara.
t.3.20.7: And those fourteen brave and fearsome rākṣasas were sent by you, for my sake, to slay Rāghava together with Lakṣmaṇa.
t.3.20.8: But all of them, full of fury, with spears and battle-axes in their hands, were struck down in battle by Rāma with arrows that pierced their vital parts.
t.3.20.9: Seeing those mighty ones fallen upon the ground in a single moment, and seeing the great deed of Rāma, a great terror arose in me.
t.3.20.11: Why do you not rescue me, sunk in this vast ocean of grief, infested with the crocodiles of despair and garlanded with the waves of terror?
t.3.20.10: Here I am, O night-wanderer, frightened, deeply agitated and dejected, and I have come to you once more for refuge, seeing danger on every side.
t.3.20.12: And these flesh-eating rākṣasas who followed in my track have been struck down to the ground by Rāma with sharpened arrows.
t.3.20.13: If you have compassion for me and for those rākṣasas, and if you have the strength and the might to contend with Rāma, O night-wanderer, then slay that thorn to the rākṣasas who has made his dwelling in the Daṇḍaka forest.
t.3.20.14: If you do not slay Rāma, my enemy, this very day, then I, shameless, will give up my life right before your eyes.
t.3.20.15: By my reasoning I perceive that you are not able to stand face to face in battle with Rāma, bow in hand, in the great combat.
t.3.20.16: You fancy yourself a hero, but you are no hero; your valour is falsely ascribed to you, since you cannot kill those two men, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa.
t.3.20.17: Depart quickly from Janasthāna together with your kinsmen! For one so lacking in courage and of such little valour as you, what kind of dwelling can there be here?
t.3.20.18: Overpowered by the splendour of Rāma, you will surely perish swiftly, for that Rāma, son of Daśaratha, is endowed with fiery might, and so is his brother of great valour, by whom I have been disfigured.
